classification.difficultyReason: Resolve an inverse-tangent launch angle into exact components, then integrate twice using initial conditions.

content.prompt:
A ball is thrown from the origin with speed $40$ m/s at $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)$ above the horizontal. Take $g=10$ m/s².

Derive the six equations and write $\mathbf r$ in vector form.

answer.short:
$a_x=0$, $a_y=-10$, $v_x=32$, $v_y=24-10t$, $x=32t$, $y=24t-5t^2$.

$\mathbf r=32t\mathbf i+(24t-5t^2)\mathbf j$ m, with $t$ in seconds.
answer.worked:
Take the launch point as the origin, with upward positive. Acceleration is in m/s², velocity in m/s and displacement in metres.

$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac34\right)\\ \sin\theta&=\frac35\\ \cos\theta&=\frac45\\ u_x&=40\cos\theta=40\cdot\frac45=32\\ u_y&=40\sin\theta=40\cdot\frac35=24\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}a_x&=0\\ a_y&=-10\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dv_x}{dt}&=0\\ v_x&=C_1\\ v_x(0)&=32\\ C_1&=32\\ \boxed{v_x=32}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dv_y}{dt}&=-10\\ v_y&=-10t+C_2\\ v_y(0)&=24\\ C_2&=24\\ \boxed{v_y=24-10t}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dx}{dt}&=v_x=32\\ x&=32t+C_3\\ x(0)&=0\\ C_3&=0\\ \boxed{x=32t}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dt}&=v_y=24-10t\\ y&=24t-5t^2+C_4\\ y(0)&=0\\ C_4&=0\\ \boxed{y=24t-5t^2}\end{aligned}$$

$$\boxed{\mathbf r=32t\mathbf i+(24t-5t^2)\mathbf j}$$
